text:
jess (AE): Hey team, new POC asks — customer wants us to explicitly exclude certain regions from egress for the tenant (no EU west1 nor APAC east1). They still want failover to US regions only. Can we support a per-tenant routing exception like that?

sam (SE): Short answer: yes, in principle. We already have policy routing by tenant+region but need to check subprocessor/KMS impacts. Who owns the routing policy config for Dedicated vs Hosted?

marco-ops: For Hosted this is a routing-rule change + subproc mapping. We can add a tenant-level denylist for region tags and a preferred-regions list for failover. Need to confirm whether any customer data touches EU KMS or subprocessors during onboarding.

jess (AE): They're on Hosted. Sales asked for the impact on price and timeline — they want to include this in the SOW. Also they asked for a short config snippet to show ops team.

ryan-infra: Pricing: excluding regions reduces our placement options so it can slightly increase average cost per request if traffic is forced into higher-cost regions. I'd estimate +8-15% on committed capacity pricing for Dedicated equivalent; for Hosted we can include an egress-affinity surcharge line item. Timeline: ~3 business days to validate, ~1 week to bake a canary for the denylist rule.

sam (SE): Config snippet (example tenant routing policy):

```
tenant: tenant-acme-corp
routing:
  deny_regions: [eu-west1, asia-east1]
  preferred_regions: [us-west1, us-central1]
  failover_policy: prefer_preferred_then_any
```

This enforces a denylist and forces failover to preferred regions only.

marco-ops: Important: we must confirm subprocessors list for the US targets. If any third-party tracing/KMS endpoints are in EU/APAC they must be disabled for this tenant. Otherwise data path could still touch those locations.

legal-joe: Can you paste the customer's questionnaire excerpt about residency? Also need to know if they require subprocessor attestations. If they require contractual subprocessor restrictions we may need legal review.

jess (AE): Pasting the ask here: "No customer data (including telemetry and logs) may leave the US for any tenant under this contract. No EU/APAC subprocessors may process data for this tenant."

marco-ops: Ok that's stricter. For Hosted we can set tenant-level controls for model inference placement and disable integrations that route telemetry to non-US endpoints. But full guarantee requires: 1) disabling third-party telemetry, 2) ensuring KMS keys are in US region and not backed by cross-region replication, 3) certifying that any managed subprocessor list excludes EU/APAC entries for this tenant. Ops can produce a technical attestation doc if legal needs it.

ryan-infra: KMS note: we can create tenant-scoped keys in us-east1 and us-west1. We need to ensure CMK policy prevents auto-replication. That is doable but will need engineering sign-off.

jess (AE): Great — customer also wants a one-page summary for the AE pack (timeline + cost delta + blockers). Who can draft?

sam (SE): I can draft the tech summary (routing behaviour + config snippet + infra notes). Marco can add ops checklist. Ryan add KMS bullet. Legal-joe can add required contractual language. I’ll aim to drop a draft by EOD tomorrow.

marco-ops: I'll run a quick runbook: steps to validate Hosted tenant denylist, telemetry toggle, subproc check. Expect ~3 business days for full ops validation.

legal-joe: Heads-up: if they demand absolute geo-lock (no visibility or storage outside US even for monitoring) we may need a custom contract amendment and may have to disallow some features (e.g., remote debugging with vendor X). I can prepare fallback language.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] New canary routing policy branch created: refs/tenant-routing/2945678901-exemption. CI triggered. :white_check_mark:

jess (AE): thanks all — will keep customer updated. Tagging @sam (SE) and @marco-ops for draft handoff. :thumbsup:
